issue.description:
Two false positives of generic-api-key block every commit and every agent Stop in /home/coding/commitgraph (commits there blocked since the hooks were installed 2026-09-28; 13 tracked files uncommitted as of 2026-10-02).

Both are in bead text inside .beads/checkpoint/forensic.jsonl (bead commitgr-6dfbd2ef), verified without printing values: no opaque token of 32+ chars on either flagged line.
1. Scheme colon: keyword 'token', then within 32 bytes the ':' of 'https:' inside 'auths["https://index.docker.io/v1/"]'. The rule takes ':' as the operator and '//index.docker.io/v1/' as the value (21 bytes, alpha+digit, entropy 3.54).
2. Prose comma: keyword 'token', then '... works (tags/list, <image>/0.9.4'. The ',' inside a parenthetical is taken as the operator and an image name plus semver as the value (15 bytes, entropy 3.64).

Fix (src/detector.rs detect_generic_assignment), narrow so no existing true positive is lost:
- A value beginning with '//' is the remainder of a URL, not a credential: skip.
- ',' counts as an operator only in the tuple form (keyword, optional identifier suffix, optional quote, comma), i.e. when the bytes between keyword and comma are identifier, quote or whitespace bytes. Parentheses, slashes or other punctuation in between mean prose.

Acceptance: unit tests for both shapes (synthetic text built at runtime) pass, the existing detector tests still pass, 'secret = <synthetic>' and a quoted tuple still detect, cargo fmt/clippy/test clean, research/rule-coverage.md updated, version bumped, installed binary reports 0 findings for commitgraph --worktree.
issue.title: generic-api-key false positives: URL scheme colon and prose comma treated as assignment operators
